title: A localization of a localization is a localization
statement: Say that a homomorphism of commutative rings $\varphi:R\to S'$ is a *localization of $R$ at* a multiplicative subset $M\subseteq R$ if (a) $\varphi(m)$ is a unit for every $m\in M$, (b) every element of $S'$ is $\varphi(x)\varphi(m)^{-1}$ with $x\in R$, $m\in M$, (c) $\varphi(x)=0$ implies $mx=0$ for some $m\in M$; then $a/m\mapsto\varphi(a)\varphi(m)^{-1}$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $M^{-1}R\cong S'$. Let $R$ be a commutative ring. (1) Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a localization of $R$ at $M$, $N\subseteq S$ a multiplicative subset and $\psi:S\to T$ a localization of $S$ at $N$. Then $U=\{x\in R:\varphi(x)=n\varphi(m)\text{ for some }n\in N,\ m\in M\}$ is a multiplicative subset of $R$, $\psi\circ\varphi:R\to T$ is a localization of $R$ at $U$, and so $T\cong U^{-1}R$ as $R$-algebras. (2) Let $M\subseteq N$ be multiplicative subsets of $R$, $\varphi:R\to S$ a localization at $M$, $\varphi':R\to T$ a localization at $N$ and $\chi:S\to T$ a ring map with $\chi\circ\varphi=\varphi'$. Then $\chi$ is a localization of $S$ at the multiplicative subset $\varphi(N)$.
